title: Visualization Library Comparison
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Compare Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly side by side, pick a need from a list to see which library fits and why, and view a typical chart of the same data in each library's default look.

learningObjectives: Students will be able to compare Matplotlib, Seaborn, and Plotly and explain which library suits a given visualization need.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Side-by-side comparison with a decision guide and a worked example on shared data
keyQuestions: Why might you choose Matplotlib for a printed report even though it takes more code?
What did Seaborn add to the chart that the other two examples did not have?
What can a reader do with the Plotly chart that is impossible with a static image?
commonMisconceptions: One library is simply the best (each fits different needs, and they are often used together).
Seaborn replaces Matplotlib (Seaborn is built on Matplotlib and its charts can be adjusted with Matplotlib commands).
An interactive chart is always better (a printed page needs a static image).
Matplotlib charts can never be zoomed (they can in an interactive window, but a saved or inline figure is a static image).
assessmentOpportunities: Students are given three short project descriptions (a figure for a science fair poster, a first look at a survey dataset, and a chart for a class web page) and name the library they would use for each with a one-sentence reason.
